career_ladder.note: Judicial officers in Odisha are governed by the Odisha Superior Judicial Service and Odisha Judicial Service Rules, 2007 (consolidated with amendments up to 2026) and the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) uniform pay matrix as mandated by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India. Officers begin as Civil Judge (Junior Division) / Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) and progress through Assured Career Progression (ACP) increments at 5-year and 10-year intervals and promotional cadres up to the High Court of Orissa.

exam_scheme.note: Governed by Rule 15 and Appendix-D of the Odisha Superior Judicial Service and Odisha Judicial Service Rules, 2007 (consolidated with amendments up to 2026). The selection process comprises Preliminary Written Examination (100 objective questions, 100 marks, 90 minutes, 25% negative marking), Main Written Examination (2 compulsory papers of 150 marks each + 3 optional papers of 150 marks each selected from 5 law disciplines = 750 marks), and Interview / Viva-Voce (100 marks), yielding a grand total of 850 marks for final ranking.

stages.source_label: Odisha Superior Judicial Service and Odisha Judicial Service Rules, 2007 (Appendix-D & Rule 23-A)

papers.paper_name: Preliminary Written Examination in Law (Constitution of India, CPC 1908, CrPC 1973/BNSS 2023, Evidence Act 1872/BSA 2023, IPC 1860/BNS 2023, Limitation Act, Transfer of Property Act, Contract Act, Law of Succession, Specific Relief Act, DV Act 2005)
papers.negative_marking: 0.25 marks (25%) deducted for each incorrect answer; computerized evaluation
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% marks for General/SEBC and minimum 35% marks for SC/ST/PwBD under Rule 23-A; marks not counted for final ranking

stages.source_label: Odisha Superior Judicial Service and Odisha Judicial Service Rules, 2007 (Appendix-D)

papers.paper_name: Compulsory Paper 1 — General English (Translation & Retranslation of 10 lines each, Short Essay of 150 words, Précis Writing of 300 words, Passage of 500 words with 5 questions)
Compulsory Paper 2 — Procedural Laws (Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 & BNSS 2023, Code of Civil Procedure 1908, Indian Evidence Act 1872 & BSA 2023)
Optional Paper (Choice 1 of 5) — Law of Crime & Law of Torts
papers.qualifying_threshold: Candidate chooses any 3 of 5 optional disciplines; minimum 33% required per paper and 45% aggregate in Main written

papers.paper_name: Optional Paper (Choice 2 of 5) — Personal Laws (Hindu Law & Mohammedan Law)

papers.paper_name: Optional Paper (Choice 4 of 5) — Law of Contract (Indian Contract Act 1872, Sale of Goods Act 1930, Partnership Act 1932, Negotiable Instruments Act 1881)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Candidate chooses any 3 of 5 optional disciplines; minimum 33% required per paper and 45% aggregate in Main written

papers.paper_name: Optional Paper (Choice 5 of 5) — Jurisprudence and The Constitution of India

papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% marks (40 marks out of 100) mandatory in viva-voce for inclusion in the final merit list under Appendix-D; candidates shortlisted in 1:3 ratio based on Main written marks

financial_package.note: Judicial officers in Odisha receive compensation governed by the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) uniform pay matrix as mandated by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India and implemented vide Government of Odisha Law Department Resolution No. 11636/L dated 26.10.2022. Level J-1 is ₹77,840 - ₹1,36,520 with judicial perks and allowances.
financial_package.pay_source_label: Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) & Law Department Resolution No. 11636/L
financial_package.estimate_note: Gross salary computed from Level J-1 entry basic ₹77,840 + 58% DA (₹45,147) + judicial HRA (8%–16% or designated official government judicial bungalow) + judicial sumptuary, robe, domestic help/home orderly, medical, and conveyance allowances. In-hand estimate reflects standard statutory deductions including 10% NPS (Basic + DA = ₹12,299), Group Insurance, and Professional Tax.
official_perks: Designated official judicial bungalow / government judicial quarters in posting district
Home Orderly and Domestic Help Allowance per Finance Department Resolution No. 21451/F dated 30.07.2024 and High Court of Orissa Office Order
Comprehensive medical facilities and reimbursement under Odisha Judicial Officers (Medical Attendance) Order 2013 & Amendment Order 2025
Sumptuary allowance and robe allowance per Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) recommendations
Conveyance allowance / official judicial vehicle with driver and fuel entitlement
Electricity and water charge reimbursement up to prescribed monthly units and mobile phone handset retention per High Court Guidelines 2026
